title: Seed-and-Stitch EKS control plane Terraform module (phased KMS/cert rotation + health-runner)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (codename: seed-and-stitch) to provision Redwood Private EKS control planes inside customer VPCs. The module must support an immutable 'seed' bootstrap, phased stitching of control plane members into a production fleet, integrated preflight validations, and automated phased KMS / TLS certificate rotation. It should be operatorless by default (works with our existing provisioner) and provide optional hooks for operator-based deployments. The module will expose a clear inputs/outputs contract for RBAC/IAM, KMS key aliases, control-plane networking boundaries, and observability endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Module is published under modules/seed-and-stitch with semantic versioning and README examples for single-tenant and cross-account KMS setups.
Provisioning path: seed bootstrap -> health-runner validation -> stitch into fleet completed in canary mode, with automated rollback on health gate failure.
All preflight checks (VPC CIDR, route tables, endpoint reachability, KMS policy, IAM role trust) are idempotent and fail fast with clear remediation messages.
Phased KMS/TLS rotation runbook and automation are documented and can be executed with a single 'apply' variable to trigger a staged rotation with health gates.
Module outputs include control_plane_endpoint, kubeconfig_secret_arn, kms_key_alias, rotation_state_arn, and monitoring_dashboard_url.
Integration tests in CI cover: idempotent re-applies, simulated network failure during stitch, and certificate rotation smoke tests.
Security review sign-off completed and module passes static TFSEC and policy-as-code checks.
Performance: control plane bootstrap completes within expected time budget across supported instance families documented in the README.
Telemetry: create CloudWatch/Datadog meters for probe latency, stitch success rate, and rotation duration.
Module is consumable by Private on-prem packaging (minimal cloud-specific assumptions) and has a documented shim for air-gapped installs.
design_decisions: Use immutable seed cluster pattern: create temporary seed control plane to run provider-managed CRs and bootstrap secrets, then stitch workload control plane nodes to target fleet.
Operatorless default: prefer Terraform-driven primitives and Lambdas for health-runner to avoid requiring an in-cluster operator unless customer opts in.
Phased rotations enforce health gates via CloudWatch alarms and step functions (orchestrator) to allow automated rollback on regression.
KMS keys are created with a customer-aliased alias and explicit grants to delegated accounts rather than broad account-level permissions.
All sensitive outputs are written to customer KMS-encrypted SecretsManager entries and never logged in plaintext in CI.
Provide optional reconciliation-mode toggles: 'self-heal' for Dedicated fleets vs 'read-only' for stricter enterprise air-gapped installs.
implementation_steps: Implement preflight validations as null_resource triggers that run small Lambda/StepFunction probes to check network and IAM; provide clear error codes.
Health-runner: implement a small Lambda that runs kube-probes and posts to an SNS topic; wire SNS->stepfunction to control stitch progression.
Implement rotation orchestration using Step Functions with checkpoints emitted to DynamoDB for idempotency and resumption.
Write comprehensive examples: single-account, cross-account KMS aliasing, and air-gapped shim with local HSM placeholder.
Add Terraform unit tests using terratest and CI jobs to exercise the module in staging AWS account (ephemeral resources cleanup).
Add TFSEC/policy checks and a pre-merge pipeline to prevent insecure defaults from being merged.
Author runbooks: manual rollback procedure, post-mortem checklist, and on-call escalation mapping to SRE.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: KMS key misconfiguration could block certificate rotation. Mitigation: implement a 'dry-run' KMS grant validator that simulates encrypt/decrypt path and fails early.
Risk: Rolling rotation may cause brief control plane instability. Mitigation: enforce stricter probe SLAs during rotation, limit concurrency, and provide automatic rollback on probe failure.
Risk: Module complexity could increase support burden. Mitigation: provide opinionated defaults and a 'simple' wrapper that hides advanced flags for typical teams.
Risk: Customer air-gapped installs might not support Lambdas/StepFunctions. Mitigation: include an operator-mode that runs the health-runner as a Kubernetes Job and a manual rotation trigger path.
test_plan: Unit tests for variable validation and output shapes.
Terratest integration to create seed cluster, run health checks, stitch into fleet, then destroy.
Simulated failure tests: kill network interface during stitch, fail KMS decrypt, and ensure rollback path triggers.
Load test the health-runner probes with synthetic traffic to verify they scale and do not exceed Lambda duration limits.
Security scanning: run tfsec, checkov, custom policy enforcement and ensure no IAM wildcard grants are introduced.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: merge module with feature flag behind 'seed_and_stitch_beta' and document in infra-team channel.
Phase 1: internal dogfood in dev org on non-critical namespaces (10% of new private clusters for 2 weeks).
Phase 2: widen to staging (50%), monitor stitch success rate, probe latency, and rotation duration for two weeks.
Phase 3: enable in production restricted to new accounts and keep legacy path available via explicit opt-in flag.
Rollback: if stitch success rate drops below 98% over 15 minute window, stepfunction triggers rollback and an incident runbook is automatically paged.
